problems.with: rather than read a speech that has already decided what every part will say.

problems.what: notice one thing; a small, believable invitation; an act of care
problems.replace: an accurate noticing and an invitation (or an act, or asking for more time).
problems.with: an accurate noticing of one thing and a small, believable invitation (or an act of care, or more time).

problems.what: 'just one thing' is new; you don't need to fill every category; acknowledge only what actually happens
problems.replace: You are inviting it to do just one thing. Then acknowledge what happens and wait.
problems.with: It doesn’t have to fill every one of those. Then acknowledge only what actually happens, and wait.

problems.what: a sensation can lead to an image, a gesture, a feeling or words (not 'respond in any way comfortable for the part')
problems.replace: Your invitation can be to respond to your noticing in any way that is comfortable for the part: with a sensation, an image, an action, a feeling, or words.
problems.with: A sensation can lead to an image, a gesture, a feeling, or words.

problems.what: the example: my chest tightened when I imagined asking for help
problems.replace: Somedays it may be best to begin with, for instance, "I notice that...."
problems.with: Say you notice, "My chest tightened when I imagined asking for help." Start with that,

problems.what: the script for the tightening
problems.replace: rather than, for instance, "This must be an abandoned child / a protective mechanism."
problems.with: rather than deciding, "This must be an abandoned child / a protective mechanism." Then you might say: "And as I notice that tightening, I can give myself a little time before deciding what it means … and notice whether there’s something I’d like to say, change, or simply stay with."

problems.what: that's enough language for one invitation; a plain 'What happens next?'; keep the words when they help
problems.replace: Somedays it may be best to say "Then I listen." And to use no more language. Somedays it may even be best to not use any language at all while some feeling is developing. Somedays not, of course.
problems.with: Then listen. That’s enough language for one invitation. A plain "What happens next?" may be better than an elegant sentence. Somedays it may even be best to not use any language at all while some feeling is developing, and somedays the words help you understand, so keep them.

problems.what: pause the words if that gives a developing feeling room (not 'no language at all')
problems.replace: Somedays it may even be best to not use any language at all while some feeling is developing,
problems.with: While a feeling is developing, it may be best to pause the words if that gives it room,

problems.what: firmness when that's the help you chose, with the published script; directness focuses attention without deciding the answer
problems.replace: Somedays it may be best to be quite firm with yourself, and say, for instance, "I am not going to let myself explain this away by saying that..."
problems.with: Somedays, when that’s the help you chose, it may be best to be quite firm with yourself: "Let the explanation wait a moment. What do I feel as I say that?" Being direct can focus your attention without deciding the answer.

problems.what: when you remain present, can change direction and want to continue, sadness or tension alone doesn't require an exit
problems.replace: If you can remain with a feeling long enough to change its direction, and if you then want to continue, it's not always necessary to have the feeling be pleasant in order for you to stay with it. Sadness and tension can sometimes be ok, if you know that you can leave, if you want to.
problems.with: If you’re still present, can change direction, and want to continue, sadness or tension on its own doesn’t mean you have to stop. It can be ok to stay.

problems.what: you can be firmer (a permission)
problems.replace: Somedays, when that’s the help you chose, it may be best to be quite firm with yourself:
problems.with: When that’s the help you chose, you can be quite firm with yourself:

problems.what: a difficult feeling needn't become pleasant before you stay with it
problems.replace: Somedays it may be best simply to focus yourself on a feeling, rather than waiting until it has become pleasant.
problems.with: You can simply stay with a difficult feeling, rather than waiting until it has become pleasant.

problems.what: 'when you're communicating' is new
problems.replace: When you're communicating your understanding of a situation, it can be useful
problems.with: It can be useful

problems.what: the three questions
problems.replace: Some useful questions to ask when you're not sure if something is a notice or a meaning:
problems.with: When it helps, ask: "What did I notice? What did it seem to mean? What supports or challenges that meaning?"

problems.what: keep apart (an instruction); you don't need to prove which came first
problems.replace: It can be useful to separate
problems.with: Keep apart

problems.what: you don't need to prove which came first
problems.replace: This is not required or always useful, and the boundaries between the three are fuzzy.
problems.with: The boundaries between the three are fuzzy, and you don’t need to prove which came first.

problems.what: an example that models the wrong move; lost: even as a wordless certainty, ask what they did, what cues, what else explains the alarm
problems.replace: You can use notices to analyze meanings ("It made my stomach tight, and I think that means they're evil"), but it's ok
problems.with: (even if it came as a wordless certainty). Ask what they actually did, what cues you noticed, and what else could explain the alarm. It's ok

problems.what: feelings deserve attention; their meanings stay open to analysis
problems.replace: Feelings are something to explore and analyze, not necessarily to accept.
problems.with: Feelings deserve attention, and what they mean is still open to analysis.

problems.what: 'sometimes it can be useful to separate these, sometimes not' (and a repeat of B8)
problems.replace: Is it a notice or a meaning? Sometimes it can be useful to separate these, sometimes not.
problems.with: Is it a notice or a meaning?

problems.what: garbled; the published: two different observations, tightening doesn't explain itself, an explicit no needs no justification, change the approach, don't repeat more persuasively
problems.replace: There is a difference between "my shoulders tightened" and "what you just said is not right". If the first: what is happening? Is this a good fit for me? If the second: you don't have to say anything else, this is not a good fit for me, say it differently or don't try again.
problems.with: There is a difference between "my shoulders tightened" and "that wording feels wrong". Tightening on its own doesn't explain itself: ask what happened, and whether the invitation fits. A clear no doesn't need any more reasons; change the words, the pace, or the approach, and don't repeat the unwelcome suggestion more persuasively.

problems.what: the script
problems.replace: First: what is happening? Is this a good fit for me? Or should I leave it be or say it differently?
problems.with: I notice the tightness. I can leave it as it is for a moment. Does this invitation fit, or would I prefer something different?

problems.what: garbled; the published: the sentence was wrong, or an unfamiliar possibility brings a feeling worth meeting; no need to decide first; skepticism isn't automatically a protector; silence isn't proof
problems.replace: Well sometimes it is the second. Or, it's something that I hadn't considered, and need to explore more, and my skepticism is not helping. But sometimes it is not helping. Sometimes there's nothing happening that I'm not aware of.
problems.with: Sometimes the sentence was simply wrong. Sometimes it's something I hadn't considered, and the feeling is worth meeting. I don't have to decide which before I make space to find out. Skepticism isn't automatically a protector, and silence isn't proof that some hidden process is working.

problems.what: garbled; the published: notice what the other person actually does before making it all an inner-child reaction; can they hear disagreement, take responsibility, make room for your experience; specific, revisable; you don't need repeated exposure to danger
problems.replace: 1. Do you perceive that the other person has a “ young inner child”, i.e. emotional immature? The key word here is “ perceive”. It does not take many exposures to a dangerous situation to learn to avoid it. Be as specific as you can. Just “ disagreeing” with you or setting boundaries does not necessarily indicate emotional immaturity.
problems.with: When another person is involved, notice what they actually do before you make the whole problem an inner-child reaction. Can they hear disagreement, take responsibility, and make room for your experience? Be as specific as you can, and be ready to change your mind. Just “disagreeing” with you or setting boundaries doesn’t by itself show emotional immaturity. And you don’t need repeated exposure to a dangerous situation before you’re allowed to protect yourself.

problems.what: notice your side too
problems.replace: 2. Do you perceive that you did something “ wrong” (feel guilty), i.e. were you manipulated? Guilt
problems.with: Notice your side too. Guilt

problems.what: did you cause harm that needs repair, abandon your position, or both?
problems.replace: Do you think that it is necessary to “ make amends” or is it “ dropping your position” to avoid the other’s disappointment?
problems.with: Did you cause harm that needs repair, or did you drop your position to make their disappointment go away, or both?

problems.what: you don't have to make someone understand before you can act
problems.replace: or cut the interaction short.
problems.with: or cut the interaction short. You don’t have to make someone understand before you can act.

problems.what: a realistic purpose for the next interaction
problems.replace: What are your aims in the interaction?
problems.with: What’s a realistic aim for the next interaction?

problems.what: when you need less, widen attention to something easier to meet
problems.replace: Also, you can always feel free to reduce the amount of what you need by switching to something that is easier for you to attend to. Pay attention to something in the room or sitting on a chair or a sound or your body.
problems.with: When you need less, widen your attention to something easier: the room, the chair, a sound, or somewhere in your body that’s easier to meet.

problems.what: let support become noticeable alongside the difficulty (not 'use it to help with')
problems.replace: This allows you to use what supports you to help with what is difficult for you.
problems.with: Let that support become noticeable alongside what is difficult for you.

problems.what: let this much be here, the support beside it
problems.replace: Ok, I will feel a little bit and notice my support.
problems.with: Ok, I can let this much be here, and notice my support beside it.

problems.what: return only when you choose

problems.with: You can always come back to this when you choose to.

problems.what: rather than a stronger induction

problems.what: return only when you choose (not 'you can always come back')
problems.replace: You can always come back to this when you choose to.

problems.what: unable to shift or stop

problems.with: you are unable to switch or stop what you are doing

problems.replace: I often find myself making it literally younger, or asking it to let me know when it is ready to tell me about its history.
problems.with: When a younger feeling shows up, I offer it company without making it literally younger or asking it to explain its history.

problems.what: without demanding that it step aside
problems.replace: I just let them know I hear that they are trying to take care of me.
problems.with: I listen to its concern, without demanding that it step aside.

problems.what: they don't each need a speech
problems.replace: I don’t need them to tell me all about themselves,
problems.with: they don’t each need a speech,

problems.what: a welcome hand placement, an imagined presence, words you'd like to hear

problems.with: a welcome hand placement, an imagined presence, words they’d like to hear,

problems.what: one change at a time
problems.replace: etc. to see what helps.
problems.with: etc., one change at a time, to see what it does.

problems.what: turned round: a comforting-sounding resource earns its place by helping now
problems.replace: If I have a resource that I know sounds comforting to that person, I bring it in.
problems.with: A resource that sounds comforting only earns its place if it actually helps right now.

problems.what: care can bring grief for what was missing; that needn't mean the love failed
problems.replace: The ‘not getting enough of something’ can cause grief. But, just because you ‘didn’t get’ enough of a certain kind of love, doesn’t mean that the love you did have was ‘bad’.
problems.with: Getting care now can bring up grief for what was missing back then. That doesn’t mean the love is failing.

problems.what: more tears don't prove more healing
problems.replace: If producing more tears doesn’t help then stop.
problems.with: More tears don’t prove more healing.

problems.what: before you decide what it means
problems.replace: Allow a metaphor to develop and then work with the metaphor.
problems.with: Let a metaphor develop before you decide what it means.

problems.what: the script: if this problem had its own image or story, what would appear, and what wants to happen next
problems.replace: “If there was something that showed up what this problem is, or tells a story about what is going on, then what would it be?” and, “what would need to happen in the metaphor?”
problems.with: “If this problem had its own image or story, what would show up?” and, “what wants to happen next?”

problems.what: try only what seems useful
problems.replace: or set a boundary, move away, do something else, etc.
problems.with: or set a boundary, move away, or take an action, only as far as it seems useful.

problems.what: or spend the session this way; let a pleasant experience grow; what it would take; hypnosis can invite something new
problems.replace: Develop a kind of love, playing, etc. that you want to have. Rehearse doing something that you decide you are going to do. Use hypnosis to develop something that you want like courage or curiosity.
problems.with: Or spend the session developing something you want: love, play, courage or curiosity. Let a pleasant experience have time to grow. Rehearse something you’ve decided to do, and notice what it would take to actually do it. Hypnosis can invite something new, not only listen to what’s already there.

problems.what: 'thanking off'; in words you can mean
problems.replace: This might include thanking off the parts or capacities you've been working with.
problems.with: This might include thanking the parts or capacities you've been working with, in words you can actually mean.

problems.what: a meal, a boundary, rest, a repaired relationship or a promise kept may matter more than another insight
problems.replace: It may also involve doing something important in your outer life.
problems.with: A meal, a boundary, rest, a repaired relationship or a promise kept may matter more than another insight.

problems.what: postpone extended checking and consequential commitments (not all checking, any commitment)

problems.with: or anything you learned that it would be a mistake to try to force, but only what actually appeared. You don't owe the notebook a complete cast of characters.
